cross_cutting.title: The typeset contract does not reach per-trace textfont - and its own checker cannot see the breach
cross_cutting.detail: _bundle_layout pins layout.font (visualizations.py:14775-14776) and rewrites annotation fonts via fig.update_annotations(font_size=font_size-1) (:14780), but it never touches per-trace textfont. The two two-panel figures set textfont explicitly on their markers+text traces - size 12 in fig_d11_haldane_chern (:15194) and size 11 in fig_d11_effective_medium (:15243) - and those values are exactly what round 3's XC-D was about: absolute pixel sizes chosen against a canvas, not ratios. Measured: 12/900*510 = 6.80 pt and 11/880*510 = 6.38 pt, versus 10 pt body text and versus 9.07/8.69 pt for the legend text sitting beside them in the same figures. The contract's own docstring for bundle_figure_typeset_pt says 'a value below ~8 pt against 10 pt body text is a Stage-9 FAIL'. SYSTEMIC PART: bundle_figure_typeset_pt(fig) computes fig.layout.font.size / fig.layout.width * 510 and therefore returns 9.63 and 9.27 pt for these two figures - a PASS - while their smallest printed text is 6.80 and 6.38 pt. The verification helper is blind to the only elements that fail. Any future figure that sets a per-trace textfont, or an axis/title font override, will be certified green the same way.
cross_cutting.fix: (a) Have _bundle_layout also normalise trace text: fig.update_traces(textfont_size=font_size-2) after the layout update, and delete the hardcoded textfont=dict(size=11/12) from both functions. (b) Make bundle_figure_typeset_pt report the MINIMUM over layout.font.size, every annotation font size, legend font size, axis title/tick font sizes and every trace textfont size - not just layout.font.size - so the number it returns is the figure's worst case.

cross_cutting.title: Plotly text that escapes the plotting area is clipped by the canvas, not wrapped
cross_cutting.detail: Both Haldane failures are the same mechanism from opposite sides. cliponaxis=False and annotation_position='top left' each push text outside the subplot's plotting area on the assumption that the surrounding margin will absorb it. In a two-panel figure the right panel's right margin is r=int(font_size*1.8)=30 px and its left neighbour is the y-axis furniture, so text that overflows is either truncated at the canvas edge (F1) or lands on top of the axis labels (F2). Neither is visible in an interactive HTML view, and neither is caught by any current check.
cross_cutting.fix: F1: shorten to 'm = 5:  C = 0 (inside)' and/or move to textposition='top left' so the string grows leftwards into the panel; or widen the x-range headroom past 8.5. F2: move the annotation inside the panel using the dead vertical space (see M4c) - annotation_position='bottom right' with the tightened y-range - rather than 'top left'. Recommend re-rendering and re-checking BOTH in the compiled PDF, since neither defect is visible in the PNG at screen scale.

cross_cutting.title: Harness output path and hardcoded canvas - answer to the explicit judgement request
cross_cutting.detail: VERDICT: a separate harness defect, NOT blocking this Stage-9 figure review - but it must not be closed as cosmetic, and it is why F3 survived to round 4. Reasoning. (1) Not blocking: Stage 9 judges the typeset result, and the shipped PNGs are correct - they were produced at each function's own canvas at scale 3 (2400x1260 = 800x420, 2700x1290 = 900x430, 2640x1410 = 880x470), and paper_draft.pdf consumes them correctly. FIGURES_DIR is PROJECT_ROOT/'figures', not papers/D11/figures/, so running the harness cannot overwrite the paper's inputs. (2) But worse than 'wrong size and wrong directory': generate_figures() calls write_image(..., width=1200, height=800, scale=2) unconditionally (scripts/review_figures.py:2336-2337), overriding each function's canvas while leaving font sizes untouched. Measured effect: phononic 9.56 -> 6.38 pt, haldane 9.63 -> 7.22 pt, effective medium 9.27 -> 6.80 pt. Regenerating through the documented command therefore REINTRODUCES XC-D exactly - the contract comment warns 'If you change width, change font_size with it or the figure silently becomes unreadable in print', and the harness changes width unconditionally. (3) The wiring is verified resolvable but has never been exercised: figures/review_manifest.json and figures/structural_checks.json are both still dated 2026-06-14 with zero occurrences of 'd11'. So the contract currently has NO automated enforcement, which is the reason a 6.4 pt label could ship into round 4 unflagged.
cross_cutting.fix: Add output_dir to FigureSpec (default FIGURES_DIR), and drop the width/height overrides from write_image so each figure exports at its own declared canvas - keep scale only. Then run the harness for D11 and let the structural check assert bundle_figure_typeset_pt(fig) >= 8.0 with the minimum-over-all-text definition from F3.

XC-E (serif) = VERIFIED FIXED, no action.

summary: Round 4 closes the round-3 blocker at the layout level and the improvement is substantial: every figure is now a full-width figure* at a measured 508 pt, in serif, with base, legend and annotation text between 8.7 and 9.6 pt against 10 pt body - legible in print, which none of them were in round 3. The func_map wiring is genuinely live, four of the five targeted MINORs are closed, all four captions are accurate, and the highest-priority anchor re-confirms cleanly from scratch three independent ways: no Berry curvature, no continuum Chern integral, no bulk-boundary content anywhere in the four figures, and the Haldane invariant is correctly shown as three discrete samples rather than a curve. Physics re-derived independently for all four figures and correct throughout, with the Chern sign, parameter point and 4x4 grid matching haldaneFrameTopo and haldaneFrame_latticeChern_eq_neg_one exactly. Three FAILs remain, all layout, all in the two two-panel figures. The typeset contract stops at layout.font and does not reach per-trace textfont, so the markers+text data labels print at 6.4-6.8 pt - and bundle_figure_typeset_pt reports those same figures as 9.3-9.6 pt PASS, because it reads only layout.font.size. On the Haldane panel the bundle's load-bearing 'inside the window' label is clipped mid-word at the canvas edge, and the flip annotation overprints the y-axis '1' tick. All three are invisible in the standalone PNGs at screen scale and were found only in the rasterised PDF, which is the same lesson round 3 recorded. Pass criterion not met.
recommendations: F3 (blocking): delete the hardcoded textfont=dict(size=12) at visualizations.py:15194 and textfont=dict(size=11) at :15243; add fig.update_traces(textfont_size=font_size-2) to _bundle_layout so per-trace text is pinned to the same ratio as everything else.

F3 systemic (blocking): redefine bundle_figure_typeset_pt to return the MINIMUM over layout.font, title font, legend font, every annotation font and every trace textfont - so it can no longer certify a figure whose smallest text fails.

F1 (blocking): stop the m=5 label overflowing the canvas - shorten to 'm = 5:  C = 0 (inside)' or set textposition='top left' so it grows into the panel; then re-check in the compiled PDF, not the PNG.

F2 (blocking): move the flip annotation off 'top left'. Tighten the Haldane right-panel y-range from [-1.9, 1.1] to about [-1.6, 0.6] and place the annotation in the freed space below the data - this fixes the tick-label overprint and the dead-space MINOR together.
M2: drop the ordinals from the D11 figure filenames, FigureSpec names, docstrings and \includegraphics paths so filename and printed number cannot diverge.

M5: give FigureSpec an output_dir and remove the width/height overrides from write_image, then run the harness for D11 so structural_checks.json finally covers these figures and can enforce the >= 8 pt floor.
M6/M4: add a vertical segment from (2/3, 2) to (2/3, 3) on the Voigt-Reuss panel so the 'exact' gap of 1 is readable off the figure.
Process: re-review round 5 against the rasterised PDF again. All three round-4 FAILs are invisible in the standalone PNGs; a PNG-only pass would have reported ALL PASS.
root_causes: The typeset contract was applied at the layout level only. Per-trace textfont bypasses _bundle_font_for, and the verification helper reads the same single field the fix touched, so the breach is self-concealing.

Plotly text pushed outside a plotting area (cliponaxis=False, annotation_position='top left') is clipped by the canvas or lands on axis furniture; in a two-panel figure the margins cannot absorb it. Not visible at screen scale.

The structural-check harness has never been exercised on D11 (manifest and structural_checks still 2026-06-14, zero 'd11'), so nothing automatically enforces the contract; and its hardcoded width=1200 would itself violate the contract if run.
